summary.short: SEC rule amending Regulation S-P requires covered financial institutions (broker-dealers, investment companies, registered investment advisers, funding portals, transfer agents) to adopt incident response programs, notify affected individuals of sensitive customer information breaches, and keep compliance records. Effective 2 August 2024.
summary.long: The amendments to Regulation S-P, adopted by the SEC, require covered institutions (broker-dealers, investment companies, registered investment advisers, funding portals and transfer agents) to adopt written policies and procedures for an incident response program covering unauthorized access to or use of customer information. The program must assess incidents, contain and control them, and notify each affected individual whose sensitive customer information was, or is reasonably likely to have been, accessed or used without authorization, as soon as practicable and no later than 30 days after becoming aware of the incident. Notice is not required if a reasonable investigation determines that sensitive customer information has not been and is not reasonably likely to be used in a manner that would result in substantial harm or inconvenience. Covered institutions must oversee their service providers, which must notify them as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a breach affecting a customer information system. The Attorney General may, by written notice to the Commission, allow delay of notice for national security or public safety reasons. The amendments extend the safeguards and disposal rules to transfer agents, broaden the customer information covered, and require written records documenting compliance. The annual privacy notice delivery provisions are conformed to a statutory exception. The rule is effective 2 August 2024.

notes: Part 1 of 5 covers the Federal Register front matter, Summary, Dates, Supplementary Information, Section I, and Section II.A (incident response program, customer notice, service providers) with the footnotes in that range. The codified regulatory text (17 CFR 248.30 and related sections) is not in this part, so the operative obligations, thresholds and definitions it sets are not coded here; references such as 'final rule 248.30(a)(4)' are discussion only. Wording of the notice deadline differs: 'as soon as reasonably practicable, but not later than 30 days' in the Section I summary of principal elements, and 'as soon as practicable' with the same 30-day outside limit in Section II.A.3.d(1). Funding portals are subject to the safeguards amendments but are excluded from the new written-records requirement (n.36). Part 2 of 5 (Federal Register pp. 47712-47724) covers the service provider definition, scope of customer information, transfer agents, notice-registered broker-dealers, recordkeeping, the annual privacy notice exception, staff statements and the compliance period; relations are limited to those stated in this part. Points for readers: (1) disposal-rule paragraph citations are not uniform: proposed 248.30(c)(1) in fn. 384, 248.30(b)(2) and (b)(2)(i) in fns. 376 and 395. (2) Commenters asked the Commission to consider preempting State breach-notice laws; the text does not state any preemption and says contract changes are not prohibited. (3) The transfer agent definition of customer applies only to section 248, per the text. (4) The compliance period (18 months for larger entities, 24 months for smaller) is stated in this part and is not coded here. Part 3 of 5 covers the opening of the economic analysis (Section IV introduction, IV.A to IV.D.1 intro, including state-law and service-provider context) and the Other Matters section. It contains no operative obligations, thresholds, events or definitions, which are annotated in other parts. Relations are cross-references to other rules, guidance and statutes, mainly for baseline and overlap; target_instrument_id is empty because no registry IDs were given. Footnote 413 states that for the economic analysis 'broker' and 'broker-dealer' exclude funding portals, unlike elsewhere in the release. Dollar and count figures in this part (e.g., compliance cost estimates, account counts) are economic estimates, not legal thresholds. Part 4 of 5 covers the economic analysis (sections IV.D to IV.F) and footnotes of the Federal Register release (Vol. 89, No. 107, June 3, 2024, pp. 47753 to 47776), plus quoted rule text (248.30(a)(4), (a)(5), (d)(5), (d)(9), (d)(10)). Quoted rule text describes the adopted amendments and is not coded here as operative obligations. Internal inconsistency: footnote 765 lists 19 entries including the District of Columbia, while the text refers to 19 States. Footnote 776 says a Proposing Release figure of 197 days should read 97. Targets not in the registry use an empty target_instrument_id. Part 5 contains the SEC release's economic, PRA and RFA sections, the Statutory Authority clause, and the rule text for 17 CFR Parts 240, 248, 270 and 275. Relations come from the authority clause and authority lines, the conforming CFR amendments, and definitional cross-references in § 248.30(d). Target instruments are not matched to registry IDs, so target_instrument_id is empty. The CFR parts are sub-units of the Code of Federal Regulations, not separate instruments. § 240.17Ad-7 is redesignated (renamed), not repealed; §§ 240.17a-4(e)(13) and 240.17ad-7(j) are reserved. Preamble references to other rules and guidance (for example Regulation Crowdfunding, Banking Agencies' Incident Response Guidance) are not coded as relations.

thresholds.note: Part 5 of 5 contains the end of the preamble (economic analysis, PRA, RFA) and the operative rule text of 248.30, 248.5, 240.17a-4, 240.17ad-7, 270.31a-1/-2 and 275.204-2. Its numbers are procedural time limits or record-retention periods (30 days, 72 hours, 100 days, 3/6 years, 60-day delays), which are coded as events or obligations, not thresholds. The small-entity size tests (broker-dealer total capital under $500,000; adviser assets under $25 million; 500 or 1,000 transfer-agent items or accounts) appear only in the RFA discussion and do not change legal treatment under the rule text, so they are not coded. No operative size, volume or value cutoff was found.
